chapter: Freelance and studio work in New York
title: Rejoining Casa Loma as the Glen Gray orchestra and the Kate Smith show
summary: O'Keefe asked him to work for Glen Gray's band, which he did for nearly five years, including a Florida stint, alongside the Kate Smith show.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: good friends. I got him to do a lot of work with us. So then let's see, I ran into O'Keefe on the street, and he asked me if I would --
That's when it became Glen Gray's --

By this time it was Glen Gray. They had Dissolved the corporation. All the guys had gone out and they bought them out and only the two of them, and now it's Glen Gray and they went down to Florida one time, in the fall, and they asked me to go down with them there, they said, 'It's a good vacation, you can get with the band, so I went down to Florida, for six or eight weeks.

This was right when the Air Corps was down there. They ran that school down there for the Air Corps -- Clark Gable was down there. I knew a guy who was pretty high up and he wanted me to enlist. I went down and tried to enlist and they wouldn't take me. Later on -- I did the 'Kate Smith Show' too, while that was going on. I did that for three years, and then when I ran into O'Keefe, 'What are you doing,' and so forth, well, the 'Kate Smith Show' was thinking about going off the air and the way things were going, I don't know. It was --
You wouldn't be able to on that show you'd be off during the summer. Get the summer replacements.
So this was a steady job and they were booked up so he said, so I went with the band. I said okay. I went with the band, they treated me well, and that lasted almost
It was after the Shaw thing. It was in the early 1940's, maybe 1946.
